subject: history
title: Crisis Years 1919-23
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace the threats that nearly killed Weimar in its first four years.
meta_desc: GCSE History Weimar crisis years — Spartacists, Kapp Putsch, Ruhr, hyperinflation.
final_note: You can now explain the political and economic crises that hit Weimar by 1923.

concepts.def: 1919 communist revolt in Berlin, quickly crushed
Right-wing ex-soldiers used against the left
1923 French invasion when Germany missed payments

walkthroughs.body_html:
In January 1919 the Spartacists tried a communist takeover in Berlin.

The government used the Freikorps — right-wing ex-soldiers — to crush it. In 1920 the Kapp Putsch tried to seize Berlin for the far right. A general strike stopped it.

Germany fell behind on reparations. In January 1923 France and Belgium occupied the Ruhr to take payment in goods.

The government called a passive resistance strike and printed money to pay workers. The result: hyperinflation. A loaf of bread cost billions of marks by November.

Hitler and the Nazis tried to overthrow Bavaria's government in the Munich Putsch.

It failed in two days. Sixteen Nazis were killed. Hitler got a short prison sentence — and used it to write Mein Kampf, spreading his ideas.

mcqs.q: Why did France occupy the Ruhr in 1923?

numericals.q: In which year was the Munich Putsch?
numericals.hint: Same year as hyperinflation and the Ruhr crisis.

free_texts.q: What was the book Hitler wrote in prison after Munich? Two words. (lowercase)
